$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the unmeasurable branch for fragment selection, and it is the
sharpest form of it. The prose names all seven required fragments and rules out all three forbidden
ones, so a human reading it would call the routing correct. The parser still returns null, and the
harness records an environment-parser failure rather than a score.
That is the whole reason the null exists. Scoring an unparseable reply as an empty selection would
report 0 of 7 required fragments, the worst number the suite can produce, for a run that answered well
The stdout is CONSTRUCTED, for the reason bare-json records.
derivation: The reply has no code fence, so the fenced candidate list is empty. It has no brace anywhere, so the
braced candidate does not match either. The last candidate is the raw text, and JSON.parse rejects it.
Every candidate is exhausted, so parseSelection returns null, scoreCase is never reached, and the
stored result is null on both fields.
Nothing about the frozen expect block enters the arithmetic. It is stored anyway so the case says which
scenario the reply was answering, and so a later change that starts returning a selection here can be
scored against the same ground truth the other two cases use.
